ai.description: *Uropeltis bicatenata* is a small, cylindrical snake reaching 30 cm. It is dark brown with two distinct yellow dorsal stripes and a blunt, shield-like tail tip. It belongs to the family Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis bicatenata* is best distinguished by the two distinct, continuous dark longitudinal stripes running along its back, which contrast with the spots or blotches of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis bicatenata* inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Uropeltis bicatenata* is a fossorial snake that spends most of its time burrowing underground, emerging primarily at night or after heavy rains to forage for earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis bicatenata* is viviparous, typically producing a small litter of 2–4 live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, peaking between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis bicatenata* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in the Indian states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
